source:
Ilse: Enrollment at Birchwood Elementary will hit 1,240 by 2030. The district grew 3.1% a year for the last five years, and the 640 new units on Quarry Road come online in 2027. We need the second wing funded now.
Raj: I get 980 by 2030. The 3.1% was driven by two subdivisions that are now built out, and the Quarry Road units are 1- and 2-bedroom apartments averaging 0.4 school-age children per unit, not the 0.9 you are using for single-family homes.
Ilse: The 0.4 comes from the county's 2019 study. Rents on Quarry Road are 22% below the county median, and cheaper units attract families. I would put it at 0.7 at least.
Raj: 0.7 still only gets you to 1,110. And the district's own kindergarten cohort fell from 168 to 151 this year. That is the leading indicator, and it is pointing down.
Ilse: One cohort is noise. The 2023 cohort was 172 and the 2022 cohort was 149. It bounces.
Raj: Then average the three: 163. Multiply by seven grades and you get roughly 1,140 without Quarry Road, and the built-out subdivisions will shed students as those families age out. I do not see 1,240 on any assumption I can defend.

extraction.mainQuestion: Will Birchwood Elementary enrollment reach about 1,240 by 2030 and justify a second wing now?

positions.label: Enrollment reaches 1,240
positions.thesis: Continued 3.1% annual growth plus the Quarry Road units will push enrollment to about 1,240 by 2030, so the second wing should be funded now.
positions.steelman: Five years of steady growth is the base rate, and below-median rents on Quarry Road will draw more families than the county's 2019 per-unit figure assumes.

groundingQuotes.quote: Enrollment at Birchwood Elementary will hit 1,240 by 2030.
We need the second wing funded now.

positions.label: Enrollment stays near 980 to 1,140
positions.thesis: The historical growth came from subdivisions that are now built out, the Quarry Road units yield few school-age children, and the kindergarten cohort is shrinking, so enrollment lands well below 1,240.
positions.steelman: The drivers behind the 3.1% rate have ended, the leading indicator is down, and even generous per-unit assumptions do not reach 1,240.

groundingQuotes.quote: I do not see 1,240 on any assumption I can defend.

claims.statement: Quarry Road units will yield at least 0.7 school-age children per unit because their rents are 22% below the county median.

resolution.condition: Count school-age children per Quarry Road unit after the 2027 lease-up.

groundingQuotes.quote: Rents on Quarry Road are 22% below the county median, and cheaper units attract families.

claims.statement: The district's 3.1% annual growth rate will continue through 2030.

resolution.condition: District enrollment counts for the next three years.

groundingQuotes.quote: The district grew 3.1% a year for the last five years
The 3.1% was driven by two subdivisions that are now built out

claims.statement: The drop in the kindergarten cohort from 168 to 151 is a leading indicator of declining enrollment rather than noise.

resolution.condition: Kindergarten cohort sizes over enough years to separate trend from year-to-year variation.

groundingQuotes.quote: the district's own kindergarten cohort fell from 168 to 151 this year

commonGroundCandidates.statement: The district grew about 3.1% a year over the last five years, 640 Quarry Road units arrive in 2027, and recent kindergarten cohorts were 149, 172, 168, and 151.

groundingQuotes.quote: the 640 new units on Quarry Road come online in 2027
The 2023 cohort was 172 and the 2022 cohort was 149.

disagreementCandidates.question: Which assumptions about growth and per-unit yield will hold through 2030?
disagreementCandidates.summary: Ilse extends the five-year growth rate and raises the per-unit yield on Quarry Road; Raj treats the growth as exhausted and reads the kindergarten cohort as a downturn.

participantStances.stance: Growth continues and Quarry Road yields at least 0.7 per unit.
Growth drivers are built out and the cohort is shrinking.

disagreementCandidates.resolutionCondition: Observe enrollment and Quarry Road household composition after 2027.

disagreementCandidates.question: Is the kindergarten cohort decline a trend or noise?
disagreementCandidates.summary: Raj reads the 168 to 151 drop as a leading indicator; Ilse points to the 149 and 172 cohorts as evidence it bounces.

participantStances.stance: One cohort is noise; it bounces.

disagreementCandidates.resolutionCondition: A longer cohort series with a trend test.

caveats: Both speakers agree on the historical figures and differ on which assumptions carry forward. None of the numbers are verified.
